questions.question: Demonstrate the use of logical operator in decision making by using suitable example. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Demonstrate the use of logical operator in decision making by using suitable example [U] / [CO1]
  • Web Development Using PHP
  • Page 2 of 6
  • Solution:
  • Logical operators in PHP are crucial for combining conditional statements in decision -making processes. They
  • allow you to test multiple conditions simultaneously within structures like if, else if, and while loops.
  • Operator Name Example Condition
  • && AND A && B Returns TRUE if both A and B are TRUE.
  • || OR A || B Returns TRUE if either A or B (or both) is TRUE.
  • ! NOT !A Returns the opposite of A. If A is TRUE, !A is FALSE
  • // Variables
  • $userAge = 20;
  • $isRegistered = true;
  • $isCitizen = false;
  • AND (&&) Checks if user is at least 18 and registered:
  • if ($userAge >= 18 && $isRegistered)
  • Output: “Access granted! Eligible to Vote.”
  • OR (||) Checks if user is either registered or a citizen:
  • if ($isRegistered || $isCitizen)
  • Output: “You have a valid status.”
  • NOT (!) Checks if user is not a citizen:
  • if (!($isCitizen))
  • Output: “User is NOT a citizen.”

questions.question: Explain the difference between traditional error handling (die(), error_reporting) and exception handling in PHP. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the difference between traditional error handling (die(), error_reporting) and exception
  • handling in PHP [U] / [CO2]
  • Solution:
  • Traditional Error Handling
  • • Passive approach using PHP’s internal mechanisms.
  • • Relies on functions like error_reporting(), die(), and set_error_handler().
  • • Treats issues as non-recoverable events (e.g., warnings, notices, fatal errors).
  • • Fatal errors abruptly stop execution.
  • • Limited flexibility and control over error types.
  • Exception Handling
  • • Active, object-oriented approach for managing recoverable issues.
  • • Uses try, catch, throw, and optionally finally.
  • • Allows graceful recovery and structured error management.
  • • Control jumps to the nearest catch block when an exception is thrown.
  • • Highly flexible — supports custom exception classes.
  • Feature Comparison
  • Feature Traditional Error Handling Exception Handling
  • Concept Errors (internal events) Exceptions (objects)
  • Control Flow Abrupt stop or ignored warnings Jumps to catch block for recovery
  • Mechanism error_reporting(), die() try, catch, throw, finally
  • Flexibility Low High — supports custom exception
  • classes
  • Best Used
  • For
  • Basic debugging, non -
  • recoverable faults
  • Professional apps ne eding
  • structured control
  • Web Development Using PHP
  • Page 3 of 6

questions.question: Explain the role of $servername, $username, $password, and $dbname in a PHP My SQL connection. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the role of $servername, $username, $password, and $dbname in a PHP MySQL
  • connection. [U] / [CO3]
  • Solution :
  • • $servername: Specifies the database server’s address — typically "localhost" for local setups or a remote
  • IP/hostname for hosted databases.
  • • $username: The MySQL account name used for authentication — often "root" in local environments.
  • • $password: The password for the MySQL user — usually "" (empty) for local setups, but should be strong
  • and secure in production.
  • • $dbname: The specific database name to connect to — ensures the script targets the correct data
  • repository.
  • These variables are passed to functions like mysqli_connect() to establish a secure and functional link
  • between PHP and MySQL.
  • PHP MySQL Connection Script
  • // Define connection variables
  • $servername = "localhost"; // or your server IP
  • $username = "root"; // default for local setup
  • $password = ""; // default is empty for XAMPP/WAMP
  • $dbname = "my_database"; // replace with your actual database name
  • // Create connection
  • $conn = new mysqli($servername, $username, $password, $dbname);
  • // Check connection
  • if ($conn->connect_error) {
  • die("Connection failed: " . $conn->connect_error);
  • }
  • echo "Connected successfully!";
  • ?>

questions.question: Explain include() and require() with examples. / [CO1] [5x5 = 25]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain include() and require() with examples. [U] / [CO1]
  • Solution :
  • Both include () and require () are used to insert the content of one PHP file into another, promoting
  • code reusability and modularity.
  • include ()
  • • Generates a warning (E_WARNING) if the file is missing.
  • • Script continues execution even if the file is not found.
  • • Best for non-critical files.
  • Example: include 'header.php';
  • require ()
  • • Generates a fatal error (E_COMPILE_ERROR) if the file is missing.
  • • Script stops execution immediately.
  • • Best for essential files.
  • Example: require 'functions.php';
  • [5x5 = 25]

questions.question: Write a PHP program to find the prime numbers between 1 and 100 using a for loop. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a PHP program to find the prime numbers between 1 and 100 using a for loop. [U] / [CO1]
  • Solution:
  • echo "Prime numbers between 1 and 100 are: \n";
  • // Loop through numbers from 2 to 100
  • for ($num = 2; $num <= 100; $num++) {
  • $isPrime = true; // Assume the number is prime initially
  • // Check for divisibility from 2 up to the square root of the number
  • // We only need to check up to sqrt($num) because if a num ber has a divisor greater than its
  • square root,
  • // it must also have a divisor smaller than its square root.
  • for ($i = 2; $i * $i <= $num; $i++) {
  • if ($num % $i == 0) {
  • $isPrime = false; // If divisible, it's not prime
  • break; // No need to check further divisors
  • }
  • }
  • // If the number is still marked as prime (and not 1), print it
  • if ($isPrime) {
  • echo $num . " ";
  • }
  • }
  • echo "\n";
  • ?>
